parts.display_text: One fission of uranium-235 converts a mass of 0.48 u into energy. A reference fuel releases 0.0048c² joules per kilogram. Calculate (energy per unit mass from the reference fuel)/(energy per unit mass from uranium-235 fission). Use 235 u as the uranium mass consumed per fission.

answer.text: Uranium yield per unit mass = (0.48/235)c². The requested ratio is 0.0048/(0.48/235) = 2.35.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Which statement about nuclear fission power stations is correct?

A. Fission generates radioactive waste that requires careful disposal
B. Water from nearby rivers is used to control the chain reaction directly
C. Control rods are used primarily to cool the reactor
D. A fission chain reaction cannot be stopped once it starts

answer.text: A. Some fission products remain radioactive and need managed storage and disposal. Control rods absorb neutrons to regulate or stop the chain reaction; the coolant removes thermal energy.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Which description best matches a suitable moderator material in a thermal-neutron fission reactor?

A. Stable nuclei with small nucleon number
B. Stable nuclei with large nucleon number
C. Unstable nuclei with small nucleon number
D. Unstable nuclei with large nucleon number

answer.text: A. Light stable nuclei can remove a large fraction of a neutron’s kinetic energy in collisions without introducing unnecessary radioactivity. A practical moderator must also have a low neutron-absorption probability.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Each uranium-235 fission releases 200 MeV. Estimate the minimum mass of pure uranium-235 needed to supply a continuous electrical output of 1.0 GW for one year. Assume every nucleus fissions and 100% of released energy is converted to electricity. Use 1 year=3.156×10⁷ s, 1 eV=1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J and one uranium-235 atom≈235×1.661×10⁻²⁷ kg.

answer.text: The required energy is Pt=3.156×10¹⁶ J. Each fission releases 200×10⁶×1.602×10⁻¹⁹=3.204×10⁻¹¹ J, requiring about 9.85×10²⁶ fissions. The fuel mass is N×235×1.661×10⁻²⁷≈384 kg≈3.8×10² kg.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Explain how energy released by fission is used to generate electricity in a nuclear power station.

answer.text: Fission products transfer their kinetic energy to surrounding material as heat. Coolant carries this energy to a heat exchanger to produce steam, which turns a turbine connected to an electrical generator.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A uranium-235 nucleus absorbs one neutron and undergoes fission to produce xenon-142, strontium-90 and neutrons. Uranium, xenon and strontium have proton numbers 92, 54 and 38. Determine the number of emitted neutrons.

answer.text: Conservation of nucleon number gives 235 + 1 = 142 + 90 + n, so n = 4. Charge is also conserved: 92 = 54 + 38.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A uranium-235 nucleus absorbs a neutron and splits into xenon-142, strontium-90 and four neutrons. The binding energies per nucleon are 7.59 MeV for uranium-235, 8.37 MeV for xenon-142 and 8.72 MeV for strontium-90. Calculate the energy released per fission.

answer.text: Energy released = total final binding energy − total initial binding energy = 142(8.37) + 90(8.72) − 235(7.59) = 189.69 MeV ≈ 190 MeV.

original-ib26mc1a-mcq-39:whole.hint: A moderator must slow neutrons efficiently while leaving them available to cause further fission.
notes: Neutrons transfer energy efficiently to nuclei of comparable mass during collisions, favouring a small nucleon number.
Moderation and control-rod absorption serve different purposes. Small stable nuclei alone are not sufficient; low neutron absorption also matters in choosing a real material.

original-ib26mb2-written-9-ei:whole.hint: Convert the plant’s power and operating time into energy, then divide by the energy from one fission.
notes: Minimum mass uses complete fuel consumption and perfect conversion. A real station needs more fuel for the same electrical output because efficiency is below 100%.
MeV is an energy per fission, not per mole or kilogram. First find the number of fissions and then multiply by the supplied single-atom mass.

original-ib26mb2-written-9-eii:whole.hint: Trace the energy from the moving fission products through the reactor’s heat-transfer system to the generator.
notes: The reactor supplies thermal energy; electricity is produced by the turbine-driven generator. Fission fragments do not directly flow through the external electrical circuit.
Distinguish the coolant and heat exchanger from the moderator and control rods. The latter manage neutron behaviour and reaction rate rather than performing the main heat-transfer step.
